title: Picard obstruction sequence for a square-zero thickening of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $j:Z\hookrightarrow Z'$ be a first order thickening of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: a representable closed immersion, tested on schemes as in [def-weil-closed-immersion], with quasi-coherent ideal $J=\ker(\mathcal O_{Z'}\to j_*\mathcal O_Z)$ satisfying $J^2=0$ and inducing a homeomorphism on point spaces. Regard $J$ as an $\mathcal O_Z$-module by the quotient action. Quasi-coherence is on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A line module is a module on this site locally isomorphic to the structure sheaf. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(W)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of line modules on $W$, with tensor-product law. Pullback is the tensor pullback of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. There is a canonical homomorphism $\delta:\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\to H^2(Z,J)$ such that $\operatorname{Pic}(Z')\xrightarrow{j^*}\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^2(Z,J)$ is exact at $\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$. Here $H^2$ is the right derived functor of global sections of module sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$, computed by injective resolutions. In particular, $H^2(Z,J)=0$ implies that every line module on $Z$ extends, up to a specified restriction isomorphism, to a line module on $Z'$. No Noetherian or properness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DNM (lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening), middle row and its connecting map into H^2.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-first-order-ringed-description], restriction identifies the small etale sites of $Z'$ and $Z$ and presents the structural quotient on the common site as $0\to J\to A\xrightarrow{p}B\to0$, where $A=\mathcal O_{Z'}$, $B=\mathcal O_Z$ and $J^2=0$. Thus all three sheaves can be considered on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$. Its coverings and ringed pullback are the canonical ones of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model].

On this common site form $0\to J\xrightarrow{x\mapsto1+x}A^\times\xrightarrow{p^\times}B^\times\to0$. The first map is injective and additive-to-multiplicative because $(1+x)(1+y)=1+x+y$ for $x,y\in J$, and $(1+x)^{-1}=1-x$. Its image is precisely the kernel of $p^\times$: $p(a)=1$ means $a=1+x$. To lift $b\in B^\times(U)$, locally lift both $b$ and $b^{-1}$ through the sheaf surjection $p$. For lifts $a,c$ one has $ac=1+x$ with $x\in J$, so $c(1-x)$ is an inverse of $a$. This proves local surjectivity, hence an epimorphism of abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective]. No surjectivity of $A(U)\to B(U)$ for a fixed $U$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0DNM, proof, displayed short exact sequence and the formula f maps to 1+f.

proof.text: The category of abelian sheaves has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Global sections is additive and left exact, since a compatible family of sections is in a kernel exactly when all its components are. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] to the short exact sequence from step 2. Its canonical connecting homomorphism $\partial:H^1(Z_{\mathrm{et}},B^\times)\to H^2(Z_{\mathrm{et}},J_{ab})$ gives an exact segment $H^1(A^\times)\to H^1(B^\times)\xrightarrow{\partial}H^2(J_{ab})$, all computed on the common site.

source.place: Tag 0DNM, proof, long exact cohomology sequence; derived.tex Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), (4).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-picard-h1-natural] on the common site to $A$ and $B$. It gives group isomorphisms $c_A:\operatorname{Pic}(Z')\cong H^1(A^\times)$ and $c_B:\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\cong H^1(B^\times)$, sending a line to the class of its sheaf of generators; its lines are modules locally isomorphic to the ring sheaf, as in the statement. Apply its naturality clause to the morphism of ringed topoi $f=(\mathrm{id},p):(\operatorname{Sh},B)\to(\operatorname{Sh},A)$ of the common site. Here $f^{-1}$ is the identity, so $f^*L'=B\otimes_AL'$ and $\rho=p^\times$. The inner map $f^*$ on $H^1$ is the identity: take $J^\bullet=I^\bullet$ and $\beta=\mathrm{id}$; the unit $\eta$ is the identity. Thus $c_B([B\otimes_AL'])=H^1(p^\times)(c_A([L']))$. By the ringed-site identification in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] and the restriction equivalence in [lem-sfb-space-first-order-ringed-description], this tensor pullback is exactly $j^*$ in the statement. Consequently the exactness in step 3 is exactness of the restriction map on the stated line modules, not of a different Picard convention. Write $\alpha_A=c_A$ and $\alpha_B=c_B$.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), frame-torsor identification, for locally free rank-one modules on a ringed site; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0DNM, final sentence of proof.

proof.text: Identify $H^2(Z_{\mathrm{et}},J_{ab})$ with the underlying abelian group of module cohomology $H^2(Z,J)$ as follows. The enlarged etale site of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] has terminal object $Z$ and equivalent sheaf and module categories, preserving global sections. Its module category has enough injectives by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] at its terminal object $Z$ with $\mathcal O_Z$ and $J$. Transfer the resulting canonical isomorphism back along the equivalences: an equivalence and its inverse preserve kernels, cokernels and injectives, so applying it to an injective resolution preserves both its exactness and its section complex. Denote the resulting isomorphism by $\beta:H^2(Z_{\mathrm{et}},J_{ab})\cong H^2(Z,J)$.

source.place: Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), global comparison; passage to a site with a final object uses the enlarged-site model.

proof.text: Define $\delta=\beta\circ\partial\circ\alpha_B$. These canonical homomorphisms make $\delta$ canonical. Since $\beta$ and $\alpha_B$ are isomorphisms, step 3 and the commutative identification in step 4 give $\ker\delta=\operatorname{im}(j^*)$. If $H^2(Z,J)=0$, every class of a line module $L$ lies in this kernel, hence is $[j^*L']$ for a line module $L'$ on $Z'$. Equality of isomorphism classes supplies an isomorphism $j^*L'\cong L$; taking this isomorphism as part of the extension gives the final assertion. None of the steps used Noetherianity or properness.
